name: Roti
steps: Mix the whole wheat flour and salt in a wide bowl. Add the measured water gradually, mixing with your fingers, until the flour comes together; flour brands absorb different amounts.
Knead for 5–7 minutes until the dough feels soft, smooth and pliable rather than crumbly or sticky. Cover and rest for 15 minutes so it becomes easier to roll.
Divide into equal balls, allowing about two rotis per base adult serving. Keep the waiting dough covered. Lightly dust the work surface with flour and roll one ball into an even, thin circle.
Heat a dry tawa over medium-high heat. Lay on a roti and cook until small bubbles appear and the underside has faint spots, usually about 30–45 seconds.
Flip and cook until the second side develops light brown spots. Flip again if needed, pressing the edges gently with a spatula so any pale areas cook; avoid pressing continuously or scorching it.
Move to a clean cloth-lined covered container while you cook the remaining dough. Serve warm; the finished roti should be flexible, with no raw-looking dough patches.
tips: Add water gradually because flour absorption varies.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
